newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SAS, Estonian Air may avoid flight stoppage.
newsitem.headline: SAS, Estonian Air may avoid flight stoppage.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines and Estonian Air, majority-owned by Maersk, hoped on Thursday that a suspension of air traffic between Estonia and Scandinavia could be avoided.
A temporary halt to flights may be caused by a row between Scandinavian and Estonian aviation officials over flying rights between Tallinn, Copenhagen and Stockholm.
"I am still optimistic on solving this problem as a day-and-a-half remains," Peter Alming, SAS Estonian district manager, told Reuters.
The flights may be suspended as the winter timetable between Estonia, Sweden and Denmark has to be confirmed by November 16.
The dispute began after Estonia asked SAS to cut its flights on the Tallinn/Copenhagen route to one a day from two as Estonian Air wanted to resume flights to the Danish capital.
The Estonians also refused SAS permission to boost its flights on Tallinn/Stockholm to twice from once a day.
Estonia says there is too much capacity already on these routes, an argument rejected by SAS.
"Stopping the flights would be a misfortune for both companies," Estonian Air president Borge Thornbech told Reuters.
Maersk won the right in May this year to buy a stake in Estonian Air but the privatisation also interested SAS.
"It (the flight row) may be one element of the struggle between SAS and Maersk," Thornbech added.
